notes:
26 rows on lines 95-120, one per line, with no wrapped rows and no second column. 13 are starred (lines 95, 98, 99, 101, 102, 105, 106, 108, 109, 115, 117, 118, 119), which matches the lead-in's "Thirteen stations have sent in returns" and the stated 26 lighthouses.

KEEPER COUNT DIFFERS FROM THE OTHER READER: 20 of the 26 rows name a keeper, not 18. The six rows with no keeper are Whalsey Skerries, Bressay Sound, Start Point, Cantick Head, Chanonry Point and Covesea Skerries. Three rows have a keeper but no star (no return): Holborn Head (D. Charleson), Cromarty (Robert S. Ritson) and the unstarred block of Kinnaird Head (F. Harvey), Buchan Ness (Thomas Gallie), Montroseness (Patrick E. Reid) and St. Abbs Head (Robert Seater). That makes 7 unstarred rows with keepers. A reader who counted only some of these may have reached 18.

Conventions: fragments drop the list's leading indentation but keep everything else. Each row's full stop that ends the character, or ends the row, is treated as punctuation. It is left out of character and keepers ("white, fixed", "Robert Burnett") but kept in fragments. Abbreviation dots inside a field are kept ("rev. every minute", "flash every 10 sec", "every ½ m", "int. visible", "Alex. Harp", "Wm. Gulcher"). The coast is taken from the section heading (EAST COAST OF SCOTLAND), since the list has no sub-headings. No row has a number, a type (L.H./L.V.) or any other content.

Ditto row, line 103: '"     (High) Orkney' stands for Hoy Sound (High). Unlike every other row, it has no comma between the name and "Orkney". The name is given as printed ('"     (High)').

Printed forms to keep but flag (copied, not corrected): "Whalsey Skerries" (now usually Whalsay); "North Ronaldshay" (North Ronaldsay); "Inch Keith" (Inchkeith); "Girdleness" and "Montroseness" printed as one word; "Tarbet Ness" (Tarbat Ness), whose place is printed "E. Ross-shire"; Cromarty's place is printed "E. Cromarty". Chanonry Point is placed in "Elgin", but it is on the Black Isle in Ross-shire, so this may be a printing error. The latest commit already flags Chanonry Point as a slip in the 1879 print, though for its character, which reads "white and red sectors, revolving every minute" here. Covesea Skerries in Elgin is correct. "Alex. Creig" (Noss Head) may be a misprint for Craig, and "Wm. Gulcher" (Girdleness) is an unusual surname; both are worth checking against other years' lists. Bell Rock's character, "white and red revolving", has no comma and no period given, unlike the others. Its place is printed "off Coast of Fife".
